scope: Reference-relative weight detection with exact reference renders; not aesthetic qualification. Five currency siblings are correlated.

decisions.reason: Cloud outline arc vs. the interior refresh-arrow strokes: both candidates hold the same arc-to-arrow weight relationship as R, and the arrowheads stay proportionate to the arrow shafts in each. No ratio difference visible at either size.

Outer ring vs. the Litecoin glyph: in Q the ring reads thinner than R's while the glyph's diagonal and crossbar keep or exceed R's weight, so the glyph dominates the ring. P holds R's near-equal ring-to-glyph weight; at 24px Q's glyph blocks up against a thin rim.
Outer ring vs. the ruble glyph: Q's ring is lighter than R's while the glyph's stem and bowl are unchanged, raising the glyph-to-ring ratio. P matches R on both the rim and the bowl/crossbar.

Ring vs. the N glyph. Q's diagonal and stems may be marginally heavier and the ring marginally thicker, but I cannot separate a uniform scale from a differential change at this fidelity; the 24px cells do not resolve the counters either side of the diagonal.
Outer ring vs. the rupee glyph: Q's rim is thinner than R's while the two horizontal bars and the descending tail keep their weight. P preserves R's rim-to-bar relationship.
Outer ring vs. the won glyph: Q pairs a thinner rim with a heavier W, whose diagonal junctions clot at 24px; R and P both keep the rim about as heavy as the W's strokes.

Laptop body outline vs. the base bar and the phone rectangle: both candidates keep the base bar and the phone's outline in the same proportion to the laptop body as R. Any difference read as overall boldness, not a changed ratio.

Apple body outline vs. the book's horizontal bars. Q's apple contour looked heavier to me while the book bars looked unchanged, but the impression did not hold up on a second pass and the stem/leaf are too small here to confirm.

Envelope outline vs. the ban badge's ring and slash. The badge in Q may carry a slightly heavier ring and slash relative to the envelope, but the badge is small enough that I cannot distinguish this from it simply being drawn a touch larger.

Face circle vs. the eye dots and mouth bar: Q's circle is visibly lighter than R's while the eyes and mouth keep their size and weight, so the features overpower the rim. P matches R's rim weight against the same features.

Cookie rim vs. the interior chips: Q's outer circle reads heavier than R's while the filled dots and the small ring chip are unchanged, changing the rim-to-chip balance. P keeps R's relationship between the rim and the chips.

Outer circle, the interior crossing ellipses, and the slash. Q reads denser overall with tighter counters in the ellipse crossings, but the outer circle appears to thicken along with them, so I cannot tell a uniform scale from a differential one.
Pan bowl and handle vs. the scattered sprinkle dots above: both candidates keep the handle's weight relative to the bowl outline, and the dots stay in the same proportion to the pan strokes as in R.

Horizontal bar vs. the three flower shapes: P's bar reads distinctly thinner than R's while the flowers are unchanged, dropping the bar-to-flower ratio. Q keeps R's heavy bar against the same flowers, and the 24px cells show the same contrast.

Star outline vs. the three trail dashes. P's star looked bolder with a tighter interior and Q's more open, but the trail dashes read alike across all three, so I could not decide which star weight is R's.
Corner brackets vs. the three interior vertical bars: Q's bars read heavier against brackets that stay close to R's, closing the gaps between bars at 24px. P keeps R's bracket-to-bar balance.

Wheel rim vs. the spokes and hub. P looked bolder than R overall, but rim, spokes and hub appeared to move together, so this may be a uniform scale that preserves the ratios; the spoke handles are too fine here to settle it.
Head rings vs. the shoulder/body curves: both candidates keep the small side heads in the same weight relation to the central head and to the body arcs as R.
Head ring and body curve vs. the ban badge. P's head ring looked heavier and Q's badge ring lighter, but I could not establish which pairing matches R's head-to-badge relationship.

Outer ring vs. the VS letterforms. Q reads heavier in both the ring and the letters and P slightly lighter than R in both, which is the uniform-versus-differential case I cannot resolve at this fidelity.
Repeat of the cloud row. Same reading: cloud arc and interior refresh arrows hold the same relationship to each other in both candidates, consistent with my W01 call.
Repeat of the won row. Q again pairs a thinner outer rim with a heavier W whose junctions clot at 24px; P holds R's rim-to-glyph weight. Consistent with W06.
Repeat of the cookie row. Q's outer rim again reads heavier than R's against unchanged interior chips; P preserves the rim-to-chip balance. Consistent with W11.
Repeat of the scan row. Q's interior vertical bars again read heavier relative to the corner brackets; P matches R's bracket-to-bar weight. Consistent with W16.

input.limitations: Judged only from the six sheets as rendered; I had no zoom or pixel-measurement, so each 96px icon was viewed at roughly two-thirds size and the 24px cells served mainly as a corroborating cue (counters filling in, gaps closing) rather than independent evidence. Stroke-width differences below roughly 10-15 percent were not reliably resolvable, which is the direct cause of the 9 abstains: in those rows the candidates differed mainly in overall boldness, and I could not distinguish a uniform scale (which preserves relative weights and should pass) from a differential thickening of one region (which should fail). The 4 "equal" calls mean no weight-ratio difference was visible to me at this fidelity, not that the candidates are proven identical; a small real difference could sit under my discrimination threshold. My most confident calls are the circle-plus-glyph rows (W02, W03, W05, W06, W10, W11 and the C2/C3 repeats), where a long smooth ring makes width comparison easiest; W14 rests on P's visibly thinner bar and W16 on Q's heavier interior bars, both a step less certain. Sheet 6 duplicates W01, W06, W11 and W16, and my answers there agree with the originals, which is a consistency check on repeatability but not on correctness -- a systematic bias would repeat too. All judgments are of visible weight only, independent of style preference, and I did not assume the candidates must differ.
